prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for sign_in and reorder changes, as only one test has been completed so far.
No clear effect was seen for adoption and redesign changes across 2 tests, as neither showed a significant win.
Finish and new_flow changes hurt performance across 2 tests, leading to negative effects and one test being stopped early.
Predictions were consistently too high compared to noise-corrected results across all tests.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -0.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- finish, new_flow: -3.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +0.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [choose_path, new_screen] Path Comparison Matrix New Screen: Adds a detailed comparison matrix screen right after path choice to explain differences between ready-made and custom pets. (why: Funnel shows choose_path drop-off of 23.8% and long mean time (514s) as users hesitate between paths.)
1: [sign_in, hint] Sign In Account Pet Persistence Hint: Displays a clear hint below sign-in options clarifying that signing in saves and syncs all pet data safely across sessions. (why: 8 support emails reported pets missing or reset after signing back in.)
2: [adoption, layout] Pick Friend Compact Selection Layout: Switches the pet pick selection grid to a compact card layout for easier scanning of options. (why: Adoption step conversion is 60.9% with median time 89s, indicating choice friction during selection.)
3: [home, new_screen] Desktop Visibility Troubleshooting New Screen: Adds a dedicated troubleshooting screen during waiting that helps users verify display settings if the desktop pet fails to show. (why: Support received multiple reports of pets failing to render on the desktop or the app stalling.)
4: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Progress Time Estimate Info: Enables visible time estimates and progress indicators on the pet initialization screen. (why: Waiting step takes median 201s and mean 2336s, causing user drop-off.)
5: [adoption, redesign] Adoption Certificate Mascot Stage Redesign: Redesigns the adoption certificate screen into a stage layout featuring pet confirmation details. (why: Adoption step conversion is low (60.9%) and overall onboarding completion is only 17.8%.)
6: [finish, copy] Home Intro Desktop Controls Copy Clarification: Updates text on the final onboarding screen to concisely explain primary hotkeys and interaction controls. (why: Support received 3 confusion emails on how to control, hide, or talk to the pet.)
7: [adoption, new_flow] Custom Pet Generation Help Sub-Flow: Adds a photo validation screen before adoption certification to help users avoid pet rendering issues. (why: Support received 3 emails about custom pet creation failing or looking incorrect.)
8: [home, notification] Pet Ready Desktop Notification Opt-In: Enables optional desktop notifications on the waiting screen when long pet generation completes. (why: Waiting step mean time is 2336s, leading users to abandon or forget the app while waiting.)

scores.note: New screens have historically hurt performance and this lacks support email evidence.
